'''Robert J. Gallery''' (born July 26, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[Guard (gridiron football)|offensive guard]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[University of Iowa]] and received [[Unanimous All-American|unanimous All-American]] recognition. He was selected with the second overall pick by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the [[2004 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. Since retiring from professional football, Gallery has become a mental health advocate and is the co-founder and president of Athletes for Care, a [[501(c)(3)]] nonprofit organization focused on athlete mental health, [[traumatic brain injury]] research, and [[psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy|psychedelic-assisted therapy]] advocacy.<ref name="gazette">{{cite news |last=Hlas |first=Mike |title=Robert Gallery's long journey with brain trauma reaches a surprisingly happy destination |url=https://www.thegazette.com/sports/robert-gallerys-long-journey-with-brain-trauma-reaches-a-surprisingly-happy-destination/ |work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |date=June 8, 2025 |access-date=February 18, 2026}}</ref><ref name="a4c">{{cite web |title=Join The Movement |url=https://athletesforcare.org/ |website=Athletes for Care |access-date=February 18, 2026}}</ref>

'''Robert Otis Griffith''' (born November 30, 1970) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs football|San Diego State Aztecs]]. He played 13 seasons in the NFL, mostly for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] from [[1994 Minnesota Vikings season|1994]] to [[2001 Minnesota Vikings season|2001]]. He also played three seasons with the [[Cleveland Browns]], and two seasons with the [[Arizona Cardinals]], In 2008, he retired as a member of the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. Griffith also served as an Executive Member of the [[NFLPA]] (National Football League Player's Association) for six years.

'''Robert Lee Geathers, Jr.''' (born August 11, 1983)<ref name="EdWeek">{{cite web|author=Reid, Karla Scoon|url=http://www.edweek.org/ew/articles/2000/11/22/12integrate.h20.html|title= Balancing Act|work=Education Week|date=November 22, 2000|access-date=March 30, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Georgia bio">{{cite web|title=Robert Geathers|url=http://georgiadogs.ocsn.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/geathers_robert00.html|publisher=Georgia Bulldogs|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040405102446/http://georgiadogs.ocsn.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/geathers_robert00.html|archive-date=April 5, 2004}}</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]]. He was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the fourth round of the [[2004 NFL draft]].

Geathers played his entire professional career for the Bengals and became a regular starter a defensive end in 2005, his second season in the NFL. With the Bengals, Geathers has been known for making [[quarterback sack|sacks]] and returning recovered fumbles. Geathers has many family members who played football at the college or professional level; his uncle [[Jumpy Geathers]] played in the NFL from 1984 to 1996, and his father Robert Geathers Sr. was a [[1981 NFL draft|1981 draft pick]]. A younger brother [[Clifton Geathers]] has played in the NFL since 2010 and another brother [[Kwame Geathers]] played for the [[San Diego Chargers]].

In July 2017, Geathers was selected as #48 of the 50 greatest Cincinnati Bengals players in the team's 50-year history.
